mainTopic: Can an אונן eat the קרבן פסח at night? Why eating the פסח is essential, and how long אנינות lasts on the day of burial and the night after it.
overview: Earlier, the גמרא found two ברייתות of רבי שמעון that seem to clash about whether an אונן may eat the קרבן פסח. רבא settles them by timing. If the death came before the פסח was slaughtered and its blood thrown, it is not brought for him. If the death came after, he eats at night, because eating the פסח is מעכב. The גמרא brings a ברייתא about יום שמועה as the source for this, and finds that the ברייתא seems to contradict itself. רב חסדא says its two parts follow different תנאים. רבה בר רב הונא splits it by sunset, which proves that eating the פסח is essential. רב אשי's reading is rejected as a mistake. The גמרא then looks for the argument between תנאים about how long אנינות lasts on the day of burial, and after several rereadings settles that רבי holds the burial day includes its night. רבא concludes from this that the day of death includes its night by Torah law. A ברייתא shows that רבי holds night אנינות is only rabbinic, and the גמרא begins its answer, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבא's new answer: timing of the slaughter decides
steps.stepSummary: רבא settles the contradiction between the two ברייתות. Both are about a death after חצות. One is about a death before the פסח was slaughtered and its blood thrown, and the other is about a death after.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Both ברייתות are talking about a relative who died after midday, and still there is no contradiction. One is about a death before they slaughtered the פסח and threw its blood for him. The other is about a death after they slaughtered and threw the blood for him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a different way to settle the two clashing ברייתות of רבי שמעון. The key point is when the death happened compared to the פסח service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the relative died before the שחיטה and זריקה, the man was already an אונן when the offering was brought, so the פסח is not brought for him. If the death came after the blood was already thrown, his offering is already valid. Then the only thing stopping him is the night-time אנינות, which is only rabbinic, so he may eat it at night.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this one and that one (both sources)
Midday. On ערב פסח, this is when the time for the פסח offering begins
They slaughtered (the offering)
They threw (the blood on the מזבח)
And it is not difficult; there is no contradiction

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא אָמַר: אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי אַחַר חֲצוֹת,
phrases.english: Rava said: Both this and that are after midday,
phrases.notes: "This and that" means the two ברייתות of רבי שמעון from just before, and the relative died after midday in both.

phrases.english: and it is not difficult;
here, it was before they slaughtered and sprinkled on his behalf,
there, it was after they slaughtered and sprinkled on his behalf.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי אַחַר חֲצוֹת, וְלָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer to the contradiction between the two ברייתות of רבי שמעון that was raised before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each ברייתא is about a different moment of death compared to the שחיטה and זריקה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seemed to give opposite rulings for the same kind of mourner.
steps.terutzMaskana: A death before the שחיטה and זריקה means the פסח is not brought for him. A death after means he eats at night, since the night-time אנינות is only rabbinic.

steps.title: Rav Adda asks: what was, was
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר מתנה challenges רבא. The offering was already brought, but he is still a mourner now, so why should that let him eat?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר מתנה said to רבא: If the relative died after they slaughtered the offering and threw its blood, what happened, happened! He is still a mourner now.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר מתנה questions רבא's split. He does not see why the earlier slaughtering should make a difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His point is that the slaughter and the throwing of the blood are in the past. The rabbinic night-time אנינות applies to him right now, and it should stop him from eating קדשים just as it does for any other offering.

keyTerms.meaning: What was, was. The past event does not change the present situation
Its blood

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָה לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Mattana said to Rava:
After they slaughtered and sprinkled its blood,
what was, was!
phrases.notes: He means: the offering being done earlier doesn't change the fact that he's a mourner now.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָה לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning behind רבא's second case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that a death after the שחיטה and זריקה lets him eat the פסח at night.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A past act cannot remove the mourning that applies now, so the rabbinic אנינות should still stop him from eating.

steps.title: רבינא: eating the Pesach is essential
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that eating the קרבן פסח is מעכב, meaning it is essential to the מצוה. This is learned from רבה בר רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to him: Eating the פסח is essential to the מצוה. We know this from what רבה בר רב הונא taught.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא defends רבא's answer. He explains that the קרבן פסח is different from other offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With most offerings, eating the meat is not essential, so the rabbis can forbid an אונן to eat. With the פסח, the eating is essential to the מצוה. So the rabbis did not let their own night-time mourning law stop him, once his offering was already properly brought.

keyTerms.meaning: Eating the קרבן פסח
Is essential. Without it, the מצוה is not fulfilled

phrases.english: Ravina said to him:
Eating the Paschal offerings is indispensable,
as we know from Rabba bar Rav Huna.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא: אֲכִילַת פְּסָחִים מְעַכְּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אדא בר מתנה's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing out what makes this case special: the eating of the פסח is essential.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Night-time אנינות should block eating any offering, the פסח too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because eating the פסח is מעכב, the rabbis did not let their own mourning law stop it.

steps.title: רבא agrees with רבינא
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells רב אדא בר מתנה to accept what רבינא, his teacher, told him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Listen to what your teacher is telling you.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא confirms that רבינא's answer is correct. This closes the back-and-forth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a new argument. It is approval. רבינא's reason, that eating the פסח is essential, is accepted as the explanation for רבא's split.

keyTerms.meaning: Listen, pay attention, obey
Your teacher

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: צָיֵית מַאי דְּקָאָמַר לָךְ רַבָּךְ.
phrases.english: He said to him: Listen to what your master is telling you.
phrases.notes: "He" is רבא, speaking to רב אדא, and "your master" is רבינא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: צָיֵית מַאי דְּקָאָמַר לָךְ רַבָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Approves רבינא's answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא's answer stands, because eating the פסח is מעכב.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא: if the death came after the שחיטה and זריקה, the mourner eats the פסח at night. The reason is that eating the פסח is essential, so rabbinic אנינות does not block it.

steps.title: What is רבה bar רב הונא's teaching?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which teaching of רבה בר רב הונא רבינא was relying on.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the teaching of רבה בר רב הונא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up its next move. It asks to see the source רבינא mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא only named the source and did not quote it. The גמרא now wants to see the actual text, to check how it shows that eating the פסח is essential.

keyTerms.meaning: What is

phrases.english: What is the teaching of Rabba bar Rav Huna?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to see the source mentioned in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The text of רבה בר רב הונא's teaching.

steps.title: The baraita about the day of hearing news
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches two things. For שבעה and שלושים, the day of hearing about a death counts like the day of burial. For eating the פסח, it counts like the day of ליקוט עצמות. In both cases he may immerse and eat קדשים at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: The day of hearing the news is like the day of burial for the מצוה of שבעה and שלושים. But for eating the פסח, it is like the day of gathering bones. In both cases he immerses and eats קדשים in the evening.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא connected to רבה בר רב הונא. It deals with someone who heard late that a relative died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For counting the mourning days, hearing the news starts the count just like a burial. For eating the פסח, the ברייתא treats it more lightly, like the day of ליקוט עצמות, which is only a rabbinic mourning for the daytime. So in the evening he does טבילה and eats.

keyTerms.meaning: The day one hears that a relative died
The day of burial
The seven-day and thirty-day mourning periods
Gathering the bones of the dead for reburial
Immerses in a מקוה
Sacrificial meat

phrases.english: As it is taught: The day of tidings is like the day of burial
for the מצוה of seven and thirty;
and for eating Paschal offerings, it is like the day of gathering bones.
Both this and that,
he immerses and eats sacrificial meat in the evening.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 by quoting the source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא comparing יום שמועה to יום קבורה for mourning, and to ליקוט עצמות for the פסח.

steps.title: The baraita seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows a problem inside the ברייתא. Its first part suggests that on the day of burial he cannot eat even at night. But its last line says that in both cases he eats at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא itself is difficult! You said the day of hearing is like the day of burial for שבעה and שלושים, but for eating the פסח it is like the day of gathering bones. That suggests that on the day of burial he may not eat even in the evening. And then it teaches: in both cases he immerses and eats קדשים in the evening!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds an inner contradiction in the ברייתא it just quoted. It is setting up the need for an explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why would the ברייתא switch to comparing with ליקוט עצמות for the פסח, unless burial day were stricter? That implies he cannot eat at night on burial day. Yet the closing line, "both this and that," seems to include burial day and allow eating at night.

keyTerms.meaning: This source itself is difficult; it contradicts itself
By inference. We learn it from what is implied
And then it goes on to teach

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is attacking רבינא or רבא here. This question is only about the inner wording of the ברייתא itself.

phrases.english: This itself is difficult!
You said: The day of tidings is like the day of burial
for the מצוה of seven and thirty,
and for eating Paschal offerings it is like the day of gathering bones,
which implies that on the day of burial
he does not eat, even in the evening;

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲדַר תָּנֵי: אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה
phrases.english: and then it teaches: Both this and that,
phrases.notes: Here the גמרא reads "this and that" as the day of burial and the day of gathering bones.

phrases.english: he immerses and eats sacrificial meat in the evening!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא quoted in step 6 from the inside.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inner consistency of the ברייתא about יום שמועה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first part implies that on burial day he cannot eat at night. The last line says that in both cases, burial day included, he eats at night.
steps.whyThisMatters: The answer to this contradiction will show how this ברייתא proves that eating the פסח is essential, which is what רבינא relied on.

steps.title: רב חסדא: It Is a Dispute Between Tannaim
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers the contradiction by saying the two parts of the ברייתא follow two different תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It is a dispute between תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives the first answer to the contradiction from Step 7. He says the two parts of the ברייתא do not need to agree, because each part follows a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of making the two lines fit together, רב חסדא splits them between two opinions. One תנא holds that after the day of burial he may not eat at night. The other holds that he may eat at night.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים
A sage from the time of the משנה

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
It is a dispute between tanna'im.
phrases.notes: He means the first part and the last line of the ברייתא follow two different opinions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the contradiction raised in Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the source between two different תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both parts of the ברייתא follow one opinion, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The two parts follow different תנאים, so there is no real contradiction.

steps.title: רבה bar רב הונא: Before Sunset Versus After Sunset
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא says the ברייתא has no contradiction. The last line is about events close to sunset, and the first part is about an event after sunset.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said: It is not difficult. Here, the case is where he heard news of his dead relative close to sunset, or the bones were gathered for him close to sunset, or his relative died and he buried him close to sunset. There, the case is after sunset.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב הונא gives a second answer to the contradiction. He says the two parts of the ברייתא are talking about different times of day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last line ('in both cases he eats at night') is about events that happened close to sunset on the day before פסח. In that case he may eat at night, even after a burial. The first part, which implies he cannot eat, is about a burial that happened after sunset, on the night of פסח itself.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
Here... and there; the two sources are talking about different cases
News of a relative's death that reaches him later
Close to sunset

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר: לָא קַשְׁיָא;
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said: It is not difficult;
here, it is where he heard news about his dead relative
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the last line of the ברייתא, which allows him to eat at night.

phrases.english: close to sunset,
and likewise where they gathered bones for him
close to sunset,
and likewise where his relative died and he buried him
close to sunset;
and there, it is after sunset.
phrases.notes: 'There' is the first part of the ברייתא, which implies he cannot eat after a burial.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the same contradiction. Unlike רב חסדא, it keeps the whole ברייתא as one opinion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by timing (before sunset versus after sunset)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two parts of the ברייתא are about the same timing, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Events close to sunset allow eating at night. A burial after sunset does not.

steps.title: After Sunset: What Happened, Happened
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא looks harder at the after-sunset case and asks why the חכמים would be lenient about the פסח at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: After sunset, what happened has happened!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presses on רבה בר רב הונא's answer. It points out that once the event has already taken place, there seems to be no reason to be lenient. This sets up the conclusion in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'What happened, happened' means the mourning event is already done. So why should the חכמים relax their rule and let him eat the פסח, which they would not do for other קדשים? The גמרא is looking for the reason behind that leniency.

keyTerms.meaning: What happened has happened; it is already done
After sunset

phrases.english: After sunset –
what happened, happened!
phrases.notes: The event is already over, so why should the פסח get special treatment compared with other קדשים?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines the logic behind רבה בר רב הונא's distinction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason the ברייתא is lenient about eating the פסח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once the event has happened, there is no clear reason to relax the rule for the פסח more than for other קדשים.

steps.title: Conclusion: Eating the Pesach Is Essential
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes from רבה בר רב הונא's reading that eating the קרבן פסח is מעכב. This is the source רבינא relied on.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from it: eating the פסח offerings is essential (מעכב).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason for the leniency: eating the פסח is מעכב. This answers the question from Step 5 about which teaching of רבה בר רב הונא רבינא was relying on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only reason the חכמים would relax their rule for the פסח is that eating it is so central that failing to eat it ruins the מצוה. So the leniency shows that אכילת פסחים מעכבא. This closes the loop back to רבינא's answer in Step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it; we can conclude
Eating the קרבן פסח
Essential; without it the מצוה is not fulfilled

steps.whatToRemember: From רבה בר רב הונא's reading of the ברייתא we learn that eating the קרבן פסח is מעכב. That is the teaching רבינא relied on.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the ברייתא quoted in Step 6 proves the point, which backs up רבינא's answer in Step 3.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from it:
eating the Paschal offerings is essential.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 10 and draws the conclusion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Eating the קרבן פסח is מעכב, which is why the חכמים were lenient about it. This is רבה בר רב הונא's teaching that רבינא used.

steps.title: רב אשי: 'Both' Means Hearing and Gathering
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rereads the last line of the ברייתא. 'Both this and that' means the day of hearing and the day of ליקוט, not the day of burial.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: What does 'both this and that' mean? This is what it is saying: both on the day of hearing the news and on the day of gathering bones, he immerses and eats קדשים in the evening.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a third way to resolve the contradiction. He changes which two cases the words 'both this and that' are pointing to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, 'both' was read as the day of burial and the day of ליקוט, which clashed with the first part. רב אשי says 'both' means only the day of hearing and the day of ליקוט. So the day of burial stays forbidden for eating at night, just as the first part implied, and the contradiction disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this and that; in both cases
This is what it is saying; a rereading of the text
Gathering the bones of the dead for reburial
He immerses in a מקוה

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי does not say a mourner may eat at night after the day of burial. Only the day of hearing and the day of ליקוט are included in 'both.'

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
What does 'both this and that' mean?
This is what it is saying:
both the day of hearing the news
and the day of gathering bones –
he immerses and eats sacrificial meat in the evening.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה? הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the contradiction in Step 7, separate from רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading which cases the words 'both this and that' refer to
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Both' means the day of burial and the day of ליקוט, so it clashes with the first part.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Both' means the day of hearing and the day of ליקוט. The day of burial still forbids eating at night.

steps.title: רב אשי's reading is rejected as a mistake
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רב אשי's reading cannot be right, because the ברייתא's wording does not fit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this answer of רב אשי is a mistake. After all, the ברייתא is already talking about those two cases. If that were all it meant, it should have just said 'this and that.' So learn from this that his answer is a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא throws out רב אשי's answer from step 12. It says the wording of the ברייתא proves his reading wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי said the ברייתא's last line only covers the two cases it was already discussing: the day of hearing and the day of ליקוט. The גמרא answers that if so, short wording like 'זה וזה' would have been enough. The ברייתא's longer wording must be adding something more, so רב אשי's reading does not fit.

keyTerms.meaning: A mistake, a made-up reading that does not hold up
After all, since
He is already discussing it
He should have said

phrases.english: And this answer of Rav Ashi is a mistake;
since the tanna is already discussing them,
phrases.notes: He means the two cases the ברייתא was already talking about, the day of hearing and the day of ליקוט.

phrases.english: he should have said "this and that"!
Rather, learn from this that it is a mistake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading רב אשי gave in step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב אשי's entire reading of the last line of the ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא's longer wording would be extra if it only meant the two cases already mentioned.

steps.title: Who are the תנאים רב חסדא meant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to רב חסדא's answer and asks which תנאים argue about this.
steps.simpleTranslation: And which תנאים argue about this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to רב חסדא's answer from step 8 and asks where we find this argument between תנאים. This line sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said the two parts of the ברייתא follow two different תנאים. The גמרא now wants to find the actual source where those תנאים argue.

keyTerms.meaning: תנאים, the sages of the משנה era, here meaning an argument between them

phrases.english: And what is the dispute of tanna'im?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting רב אשי, the גמרא goes back to רב חסדא's approach.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the argument between תנאים that רב חסדא relied on

steps.title: The ברייתא about how long one is an אונן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: the תנא קמא says a person is an אונן the whole day, and רבי says only until the relative is buried.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: Until when is a person an אונן over his relative? The whole day. רבי says: As long as the relative has not been buried.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by quoting a ברייתא where the תנא קמא and רבי argue about how long אנינות lasts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אונן may not eat קדשים. The תנא קמא says the אנינות lasts all day, which suggests it does not continue into the night. רבי ties it to the burial instead of to the day.

keyTerms.meaning: Is in the state of an אונן, a mourner before or on the day of burial who may not eat קדשים
The whole day
Was buried

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
Until when does one mourn acutely for him?
The entire day.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא נִקְבַּר.
phrases.english: Rabbi says: As long as he has not been buried.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 by bringing the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The argument between the תנא קמא and רבי about how long אנינות lasts

steps.title: This ברייתא cannot be about the day of death
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא is about the day of death, the תנא קמא would be saying that the night after is not included. But everyone agrees that the night after the day of death counts, at least מדרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with? If you say it is the day of death, is there anyone who disagrees that the day of death takes hold of its night, at least מדרבנן?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what case the ברייתא is about. It shows that it cannot be the day of death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא said 'the whole day,' which suggests the night after is not included. But all agree that אנינות on the day of death continues into that night, at least מדרבנן. So the תנא קמא cannot be talking about the day of death.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with?
If you say
The day of death
Takes hold of its night, so the next night is included
By rabbinic law

phrases.english: With what are we dealing?
If we say with the day of death,
is there anyone who does not hold
that the day of death takes hold of its night
by rabbinic law?!
phrases.notes: This asks about the תנא קמא, who said 'the whole day' and seems to leave out the night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what case the ברייתא from step 15 is about, and attacks the first option.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of the תנא קמא, if the ברייתא is read as being about the day of death
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Everyone agrees the day of death includes its night מדרבנן, so 'the whole day' cannot be about the day of death.

steps.title: A second problem: רבי's view on the day of death
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא is about the day of death, רבי would be saying that אנינות ends at burial, even on that same day. But everyone agrees from the פסוק 'ואחריתה כיום מר' that the whole day of death is a day of אנינות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, רבי says: As long as he has not been buried. This means that once he buried him, it becomes permitted to him. But is there anyone who disagrees with the פסוק 'and its end like a bitter day'?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second reason why the ברייתא cannot be about the day of death, this time from רבי's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי said 'as long as he has not been buried,' so after burial the person could eat קדשים even on the day of death. But the פסוק 'ואחריתה כיום מר' teaches that the whole day of death stays bitter, even after burial. Everyone holds this, so רבי cannot mean the day of death either.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore
This implies that
It becomes permitted to him
And its end like a bitter day, a פסוק showing the whole day of death is a day of אנינות

steps.whatToRemember: Both views in the ברייתא run into trouble if it is about the day of death. The תנא קמא would leave out the night, and רבי would end אנינות at burial. So the גמרא must find a different case for this ברייתא.

phrases.english: And furthermore, Rabbi says:
As long as he has not been buried.
This implies that once he buried him, it is permitted to him;
phrases.notes: Permitted to eat קדשים, even on that same day of death.

phrases.english: but is there anyone who does not hold
"And the end thereof as a bitter day"?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ, רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא נִקְבַּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge to the same option, this time from רבי's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of רבי, if the ברייתא is read as being about the day of death
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי's words suggest אנינות ends at burial even on the day of death. That goes against the פסוק that the whole day of death is bitter, which everyone accepts.

steps.title: The argument is about the day of burial
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that the ברייתא is not talking about the day of death. It is talking about the day of burial, when that is a later day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: The ברייתא is talking about the day of burial.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the two problems from steps 16 and 17. He says the argument between the תנא קמא and רבי is about the day of burial, not the day of death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees about the day of death: the whole day counts, and so does the night after it. So the argument must be about a burial that happens on a later day. On that day, the תנאים argue whether אנינות lasts only until the burial or until the end of the day.

keyTerms.meaning: The day of burial, when it is a different day from the day of death
Is standing on, is talking about

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
It is talking about the day of burial.
phrases.notes: He means the ברייתא from step 15. Its argument is about a burial day that comes after the day of death.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: אַיּוֹם קְבוּרָה קָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the two problems in steps 16 and 17 by moving the case to the day of burial.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing which case the ברייתא is about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was about the day of death, which clashes with what everyone agrees.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a later day of burial, so it does not clash with the rules for the day of death.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the night after burial still counts
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף brings a ברייתא that suggests the night after the day of burial is still אנינות. On רב ששת's reading, neither תנא would hold that view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objects: There is a ברייתא that says someone who hears that his relative died is like someone who gathers a relative's bones. He goes to the מקוה and may eat קדשים in the evening. This implies that on the day of burial he may not eat even in the evening. Whose view is this?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף challenges רב ששת. He uses a ברייתא that suggests a person may not eat קדשים even on the night after the day of burial.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hearing the news, or gathering bones, makes a person an אונן only for the day, so he may eat at night. The ברייתא contrasts this with the day of burial, which implies that night is still forbidden. But on רב ששת's reading, the תנא קמא says 'the whole day' and רבי says 'until burial.' Neither one includes the night, so this ברייתא matches no one.

keyTerms.meaning: Objects, raises a challenge
Someone who gathers a relative's bones for reburial
Goes into a מקוה
By implication, from this we learn
Whose view is this?

phrases.english: Rav Yosef objects:
But what about that which is taught:
One who hears news of his dead relative is like one who gathers bones,
he immerses and eats sacrificial food in the evening;
this implies that on the day of burial
he may not eat even in the evening;
whose view is this?
phrases.notes: On רב ששת's reading, neither the תנא קמא nor רבי includes that night.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף רַב יוֹסֵף, אֶלָּא הָא דְּקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב ששת's reading of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's reading, in which neither תנא counts the night after the day of burial
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא implies the night after burial is forbidden. No תנא on רב ששת's reading would hold that, so the ברייתא would have no author.

steps.title: רב יוסף rereads the argument
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף changes how the argument reads. The תנא קמא includes the night after the day of burial, and רבי says that once the relative is buried, the night is not included.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it this way: Until when is a person an אונן? That whole day and its night. רבי says: As long as the relative is not buried. But once he is buried, it is without its night.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף fixes the problem by rereading the ברייתא. Now the תנא קמא says the night after the day of burial counts, which fits the ברייתא he just brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this reading, the 'hearing the news' ברייתא follows the תנא קמא, who includes the night. רבי says that once the burial has happened, the night is not included. That makes רבי the more lenient one, and this point is what gets challenged next.

keyTerms.meaning: Answer, read the text this way
Its night, the night after that day
Without

phrases.english: Rather, answer this way:
Until when does one remain an onen for him?
That entire day and its night.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא נִקְבַּר;
phrases.english: Rabbi says: As long as he has not been buried;
but once he is buried, it is without its night.
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are the corrected wording.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא תָּרֵיץ: עַד מָתַי מִתְאוֹנְנִין עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rereads the argument to solve the problem raised in step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Neither תנא counts the night after burial.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא קמא counts the night after the day of burial, and רבי does not count it once the burial has happened.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: רבי is the strict one, not the lenient one
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה is surprised. רב יוסף's reading makes רבי lenient, but another ברייתא shows רבי is stricter than the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: They told this to רבי ירמיה. He said: Would a great man like רב יוסף say this? Would he say that רבי is the lenient one? But there is a ברייתא: Until when is a person an אונן? As long as the relative is not buried, even for ten days. These are the words of רבי. The חכמים say: He is an אונן only on that day.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה challenges רב יוסף's reading. Another ברייתא shows that רבי is the strict opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this ברייתא, רבי stretches אנינות for as long as the relative is unburied, even ten days. The חכמים limit it to one day. So רבי is the stricter one, and it makes no sense to read him as the lenient side who leaves out the night.

keyTerms.meaning: A great man, a great scholar
On the lenient side
The Sages, the majority opinion

phrases.english: They said it before Rabbi Yirmeya;

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: גַּבְרָא רַבָּה כְּרַב יוֹסֵף לֵימָא הָכִי?!
phrases.english: he said: Would a great man like Rav Yosef say this?!
Would he say that Rabbi is the lenient one?!
But isn't it taught:
Until when is one an onen for him?
As long as he is not buried,
even from now until ten days.
These are the words of Rabbi.
And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מִתְאוֹנֵן עָלָיו אֶלָּא אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם בִּלְבַד!
phrases.english: He is an onen for him only on that day alone!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יוסף's reading from step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's reading, which makes רבי the lenient opinion
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא shows רבי is stricter than the חכמים, so he should not be read as the one who leaves out the night.

steps.title: Final reading: once buried, the day takes its night
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה reverses the reading. The תנא קמא says the day of burial does not include its night. רבי says that once the relative is buried, the day 'takes hold of' its night.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it like this: Until when is a person an אונן? That whole day, without its night. רבי says: As long as the relative is not buried. And once he is buried, the day takes hold of its night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final reading of the argument. Now רבי is the strict side, who includes the night after the day of burial.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This keeps רבי strict, matching the 'ten days' ברייתא. It also gives the 'hearing the news' ברייתא an author: רבי, who forbids the night after burial. So this is the argument between תנאים that רב חסדא was pointing to.

keyTerms.meaning: Takes hold of its night, so the following night also counts
Was buried

steps.whatToRemember: Final reading: the תנא קמא says אנינות lasts only for the day of burial, without the night. רבי says that once the burial happens, the night after also counts. This is the argument רב חסדא meant.
steps.confusionAlert: Steps 20 and 22 swap the opinions. In the final reading, the תנא קמא leaves out the night and רבי includes it, the opposite of רב יוסף's version.

phrases.english: Rather, answer like this:
Until when is he an onen for him?
That entire day, without its night.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא נִקְבַּר.
phrases.english: Rabbi says: As long as he has not been buried.
And once he is buried, the day takes hold of its night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי ירמיה's challenge in step 21 by reversing the opinions.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reversing the opinions in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנא קמא includes the night and רבי is lenient.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא קמא leaves out the night, and רבי, the strict one, includes the night after burial.

steps.title: רבא infers that the day of death takes hold of its night by Torah law
steps.stepSummary: רבא reasons from רבי's view on the day of burial to a conclusion about the day of death.
steps.simpleTranslation: They told this to רבא. He said: since רבי says the day of burial takes hold of its night by rabbinic law, we can learn that the day of death takes hold of its night by Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: The reading of רבי from רבי ירמיה (step 22) is brought to רבא. רבא uses it to learn something new about the day of death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אנינות on the day of burial is only rabbinic, so its night is held by rabbinic law. רבא reasons that the חכמים would not be stricter in their own rule than the matching Torah law. So the day of death, whose אנינות is from the Torah, must take hold of its night by Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Takes hold of its night,' meaning the night after it is also counted as אנינות
By implication; we learn it from what was said
By rabbinic law
By Torah law
The day of death
The day of burial

phrases.english: They said it before Rava;
phrases.notes: 'It' is רבי ירמיה's reading of רבי from just before.

phrases.english: since Rabbi says:
the day of burial takes hold of its night by rabbinic law –
by implication, the day of death
takes hold of its night by Torah law;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a new inference on top of רבי ירמיה's reading of רבי from step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי, the day of death takes hold of its night by Torah law, since the rabbinic day of burial takes hold of its night by rabbinic law.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי holds night אנינות is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא's inference with a ברייתא where רבי says night אנינות is not from the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי really hold that night אנינות is from the Torah? But a ברייתא teaches: 'Behold, today' — Aharon said: I am forbidden today but allowed at night; for future generations it is forbidden both by day and by night. These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי says: night אנינות is not Torah law, only rabbinic law!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's conclusion. It quotes a ברייתא where רבי openly says night אנינות is only rabbinic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said that, for רבי, the night after the day of death is אנינות by Torah law. But in this ברייתא, רבי argues with רבי יהודה and says night אנינות is only from the סופרים. So רבא's inference seems to clash with רבי's own words.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Behold, today,' Aharon's words in ויקרא 10:19
For future generations, the lasting law after that first day
אנינות at night, the night after the death
Words of the Scribes; rabbinic law

steps.confusionAlert: Two different people appear here. רבי יהודה (a תנא) says night אנינות is forbidden for future generations. 'רבי' alone means רבי יהודה הנשיא, and he is the one who says it is only rabbinic.

phrases.english: And does Rabbi hold
that acute mourning at night is by Torah law?!
But isn't it taught in a baraita:
"Behold, today" –
I am forbidden today but permitted at night,

phrases.aramaic: וּלְדוֹרוֹת בֵּין בַּיּוֹם וּבֵין בַּלַּיְלָה אָסוּר.
phrases.english: but for future generations, it is forbidden both by day and by night.
These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi says:
acute mourning at night is not by Torah law,
but rather by rabbinic law!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי אֲנִינוּת לַיְלָה דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רבא's inference from step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that, according to רבי, the day of death takes hold of its night by Torah law.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא quotes רבי himself saying night אנינות is only rabbinic, which contradicts the inference.

steps.title: The answer begins: night אנינות really is rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא grants that, for רבי, night אנינות after death is truly only rabbinic.
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, it is rabbinic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer by agreeing with the ברייתא: for רבי, the night's אנינות really is only rabbinic. This line sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not argue with the ברייתא. It accepts that רבי holds night אנינות is rabbinic, so רבא's words will need to be explained in a way that fits this.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Actually' or 'really.' The גמרא keeps a position and explains it
Rabbinic; from the חכמים, not the Torah
'It is,' here meaning the night's אנינות

phrases.english: Actually, it is by rabbinic law,
phrases.notes: 'It' means אנינות on the night after the day of death, according to רבי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the challenge of step 24 by accepting the ברייתא's view of רבי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the challenger's source and begins to adjust the earlier inference to fit it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's inference seemed to say רבי holds that the night after death is אנינות by Torah law.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי, the night after death is אנינות only by rabbinic law. The explanation of how this fits continues in the next lines.
